answer: A bonded collateral protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock slashable tokens in an escrow vault before transacting. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of provisioning locked financial liquidity per identity. Gateways at the settlement wharf authenticate these stake proofs prior to routing service requests. A key limitation is that sudden market volatility can induce a liquidation spiral, unfairly penalizing honest agents with small cash reserves.
